definition.name: Heating assembly
definition.description: Current through the element makes heat. The immersion, floor mat and storage heater each use that principle.

terminals.label: L
terminals.purpose: Line brings power to the fitting. Its usual marking is L.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Neutral carries current back to the supply while the load is on.

terminals.label: PE
terminals.purpose: Earth connection for the fitting. The earth path stays connected when the switch opens.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The case holds the working parts in place and keeps them apart.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: Lift the cover on the bench to see the connections underneath.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: A clamp holds the bare end of a wire against the metal terminal.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: These keep the fitting in place. Look for the screws or clips that hold it.

parts.name: Heating element
parts.purpose: Current heats the element. With the same resistance, doubling the voltage gives four times the heating power.

parts.name: Thermal protection
parts.purpose: A sustained overload heats this part until the protection trips. Trip times in the lab are approximate.

terminals.label: L
terminals.purpose: Brown live core in the heater’s factory-fitted lead. This core supplies the heater controller and element.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Blue neutral core in the heater’s factory-fitted lead. This core supplies the heater controller and element.

terminals.label: E
terminals.purpose: Green and yellow earth core in the heater’s factory-fitted lead. It bonds the metal case to earth.
